assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase from the same period last year, driven by a sharp rise in reported cases.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with an 853% increase from the same period last year, indicating a significant surge in reported cases.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with an 87% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased compared to the previous year.
Global flu test positivity is peaking with a 29% increase from the previous month, and US flu hospital admissions are rising sharply.
Polio Wikipedia readership is at the 97th percentile of the past year, indicating heightened public interest but no reported cases.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1388% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased compared to the previous year.
Group A strep Wikipedia readership is at the 55th percentile of the past year, indicating moderate public interest but no specific case data.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are peaking with a 45% increase from the same period last year, though the number of cases has decreased compared to the previous year.

Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 57/100, showing a slight increase in reported cases this year compared to last year. The first locally acquired cases were reported in Switzerland in October 2026.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a score of 55/100, indicating a significant increase in reported cases compared to the previous eight months.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 54/100, showing a slight decrease in reported cases this year compared to last year.
COVID-19 hospital admissions in the US are at baseline with a score of 53/100, showing a modest increase in hospitalizations compared to the previous month.
RSV cases are rising with a score of 53/100, showing a significant increase in hospitalizations and test positivity rates compared to the previous month.
Malaria cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 50/100, showing a slight increase in reported cases this year compared to last year.
Typhoid fever readership on Wikipedia is at the 43rd percentile of the past year, indicating moderate public interest.
